text:
Alex Chen: quick sync before I head out — summary from the last 75m :rotating_light:
Alex Chen: At ~1805120200 we saw a burst of 503s from hosted inference in us-west-2. Pager fired for latency/service errors (auto page to primary).
incident-bot: [ALERT] 503 spike detected on /v1/generate (us-west-2) — 120s window, 18% error rate — pager ID PGR-8492 — links: https://redwood.monitoring/alerts/PGR-8492
Samir Patel: I picked this up. Short timeline: cache pressure on kv-shard-7 caused GC/latency spikes, which backed up request queues and hit our frontend timeout (503).
Samir Patel: Actions taken: rolled the inference runtime on the affected node pool, bumped autoscaler threshold for 10m to absorb burst, and enabled prefix cache hits for high-volume routes.
Jordan Li: runbook link for kv cache pressure is here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-pressure — follow section A (throttle -> restart -> mitigate).
Mira Gomez: Noted customer-facing impact: a handful of small customers saw degraded responses (short-lived). CS notified via CS-notifications-bot, but no SRE escalation requested by account teams yet.
CS-notifications-bot: Sent customer digest to CS channel and created ticket CS-7729 for customers with >5 failed requests in 10m.
Alex Chen: concrete commands we ran (for handover):
```
# restart inference runtime on pool-a
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime-pool-a
# check pod logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-runtime -c runtime --since=15m | grep -i "kv cache" | tail -n 50
```
Samir Patel: Current status: error rate dropped to ~0.5% over the last 10m, CPU on pool-a back to normal, KV eviction rate decreased after restart. Watching for recurrence; autoscaler pause expires in ~6m.
Jordan Li: Telemetry notes: added a short-term trace filter for traces sampling the /v1/generate slow path — will keep 1% extra for 30m to help root cause if it recurs.
Mira Gomez: Coverage note — tomorrow morning (PST) there's a 2hr gap where our coverage has only one engineer (on-call secondary is in PTO). We need to confirm backup for that window.
Alex Chen: Next steps before handover: (1) confirm secondary coverage for 0800-1000 PST tomorrow, (2) remove autoscaler override after 10m if stable, (3) follow up on CS-7729 and escalate if more reports come in.
Samir Patel: I'll stay as primary for another 20m then hand off. Leaving a link to active diagnostics: https://redwood.dashboards/kv-shard-7/active
Jordan Li: If it spikes again, use runbook section B to put the node pool into cordon/drain rather than full restart — less customer-facing disruption.
Mira Gomez: I can be backup for 08:00-10:00 PST tomorrow; ping me in #eng-oncall 15m before handoff.
Alex Chen: Thanks — final state at handoff: incident mode = monitoring, mitigation applied (restart + autoscaler bump), customer impact limited and logged, CS ticket created.
Alex Chen: Handoff recipients: primary -> Mira Gomez (1805126800), secondary -> Jordan Li. Coverage gap note documented. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: leaving a short checklist for Mira to pick up:
- verify error rate stays <1% for 30m
- confirm autoscaler back to default after override expires
- check pod restarts & OOMs: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide`
- escalate to platform infra if KV eviction rate > threshold

Mira Gomez: got it, thanks. I'll bump the thread if anything changes after I take over.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE-PENDING] Alert PGR-8492: error rate below threshold for 10m — will auto-resolve in 20m if stable.
Alex Chen: signing off for the evening — appreciate the quick response team.
